instructions: Product Lifecycle Management platform. Stack: Next.js 16 + TypeScript + Supabase + Vercel + shadcn/ui. Review against the canonical repo rules, not generic Next.js patterns. Critical rules: use bun/bunx only (never npm/npx), IDs must be Date.now().toString() (never UUID), every app query must explicitly filter by team_id, tables must use team_id TEXT NOT NULL with RLS, root supabase/ is the only canonical migration tree, API routes must validate auth and active team context, and internal admin/debug routes are internal-only tools rather than customer-facing product pages.
ignorePatterns:
greptile.json
*.lock
*.log
node_modules/**
.next/**
supabase/.temp/**
coverage/**
dist/**
build/**

other.content: This is a multi-tenant PLM app. Team context must be explicit: queries filter by team_id and authenticated routes resolve one active team context rather than assuming a single membership row. Workspaces belong to teams and are the aggregation layer over work items.

Public and review-link flows must still preserve tenant boundaries. Public routes may intentionally avoid auth, but they must only expose minimal public DTOs and must never rely on broad table reads without explicit scope constraints.

Admin and debug routes are internal tools. They are allowed, but they must be access-controlled, hidden from normal product navigation, and must not become the canonical path for schema/bootstrap changes.

rules.rule: TypeScript is strict. Flag any new any usage, ts-ignore/ts-expect-error, silent catch blocks, or missing error handling.

API routes must authenticate where required, resolve active team context for team-scoped operations, validate inputs with Zod, and preserve the repo response contract: success responses include success: true and failures include success: false.
Every team-scoped Supabase query must include an explicit team_id filter in application code. Do not approve code that relies on RLS alone when a team_id predicate should be present.

Root supabase/ is canonical. New schema/RLS changes belong only in root supabase/migrations. Tables should use id TEXT PRIMARY KEY with timestamp-based IDs, team_id TEXT NOT NULL, an index on team_id, and RLS policies scoped to team access.

Follow the canonical phase model from docs/ARCHITECTURE_CONSOLIDATION.md: Feature = design -> build -> refine -> launch, Bug = triage -> investigating -> fixing -> verified, Concept = ideation -> research -> validated|rejected. Do not enforce the older generic research/planning/execution/review/complete flow.

UI should use shadcn/ui components and Tailwind utility classes. Flag new custom CSS files or bespoke component primitives that bypass the existing UI system unless there is a clear established pattern in the repo.

files.description: Repo-level operating rules: bun only, timestamp IDs, explicit team_id filters, shadcn/ui only, and links to the canonical rule files.
Core coding rules for package manager choice, ID format, team isolation, TypeScript strictness, and UI constraints.
High-level architecture rules for workspace aggregation, work item phases, timeline status, and domain terminology.
Canonical Supabase migration/query rules: team_id filtering, RLS expectations, and bunx Supabase commands.
Canonical architecture reference. Use this over older docs when evaluating work item phase behavior, workspace aggregation, and type-specific workflows.
API route surface for auth, active team resolution, and request/response conventions.
Active team resolution helpers. Team-scoped review should align with this context model rather than assuming one team_members row per user.
Canonical migration tree. next-app/supabase/ is legacy material, not the source of truth for new schema changes.
